'''Stephen R. Hilbert''' is an American [[mathematician]] best known as co-author of the [[Bramble–Hilbert lemma]], which he published with [[James H. Bramble]] in 1970.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Estimation of Linear Functionals on Sobolev Spaces with Application to Fourier Transforms and Spline Interpolation|author=[[James H. Bramble]] and Stephen R. Hilbert|journal=SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis|year=1970|volume=7|issue=1 (Mar., 1970)|pages= 112–124|publisher= Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|doi=10.1137/0707006|jstor= 2949585|bibcode=1970SJNA....7..112B }}</ref> Hilbert's area of specialty is [[numerical analysis]].<ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web |url= http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=149812 |title=The Mathematics Genealogy Project&nbsp;– Stephen Hilbert |work=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu |accessdate=May 4, 2011}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated2>{{cite web |url=http://www.math.binghamton.edu/maa_seaway/Distinguished/disting94.html |title=Seaway Section of the MAA: Distinguished Teaching Awards |work=math.binghamton.edu |access-date=May 4, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720174754/http://www.math.binghamton.edu/maa_seaway/Distinguished/disting94.html |archive-date=July 20, 2011 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> He has been a professor of mathematics at [[Ithaca College]] since 1968.<ref>''An Introduction to Sobolev Spaces and Interpolation Spaces'', Lecture Notes of the Unione Matematica Italiana, 2007, Volume 3, 53–57, {{doi|10.1007/978-3-540-71483-5_11}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://faculty.ithaca.edu/hilbert/ |title=Stephen Hilbert&nbsp;– Ithaca College |work=faculty.ithaca.edu |accessdate=May 4, 2011}}</ref> Additionally, he taught mathematics at [[Cornell University]] as a [[Visiting scholar|visiting program professor]] during the 2003–2004 academic year.<ref name=autogenerated3>{{cite web |url= https://www.math.cornell.edu/News/2003-2004/welcome.html |title=Cornell Math – Welcome New Faculty and Graduate Students |work=math.cornell.edu |accessdate=May 16, 2011}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Hilbert was born in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York (state)|New York]].<ref name=autogenerated2 /> As a teenager, he attended [[Regis High School (New York City)|Regis High School]] in [[New York City]].<ref name=autogenerated2 /> He received his BS in mathematics from the [[University of Notre Dame]] in 1964 and his PhD in [[applied mathematics]] from the [[University of Maryland]] in 1969.<ref name=autogenerated2 /><ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.ithaca.edu/catalogs/ug0809/facadmin/school_of_humanities_and_sciences.php |title=School of Humanities and Sciences&nbsp;– Undergraduate Catalog 2008&nbsp;– 2009&nbsp;– Ithaca College |work=ithaca.edu/catalogs |accessdate=May 4, 2011}}</ref> He completed his dissertation, ''Numerical Solutions of Elliptic Partial Differential Equations'', with Bramble as his advisor.<ref name=autogenerated1 /><ref name=autogenerated2 />

==Awards and honors==
*Distinguished College Teaching of Mathematics Award&nbsp;– 1994&nbsp;– Seaway Section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]]<ref name=autogenerated2 /><ref name=autogenerated4>{{cite web |url= https://wwwcdn.ithaca.edu/file-download/download/public/35828 |title=History of Ithaca College Department of Mathematics |work=ithaca.edu/hs/depts/math |accessdate=July 17, 2021}}</ref>
*Dana Teaching Fellow&nbsp;– 1985<ref name=autogenerated2 />
*Dana Teaching Fellow&nbsp;– 1982<ref name=autogenerated2 />
*Outstanding Faculty Award&nbsp;– 1979&nbsp;– School of Humanities and Sciences, Ithaca College<ref name=autogenerated2 />

==Publications==
*''Barron's GMAT''. Jaffe, Eugene D., and Stephen Hilbert, 2009, Barron's Educational Series, {{ISBN|978-0-7641-3993-2}}, 497 pgs
*''Calculus: An Active Approach with Projects''. Hilbert, Stephen, et al., 1993–1994, John Wiley & Sons; Reissued 2010 by Mathematical Association of America,  {{ISBN|978-0-88385-763-2}}, 307 pgs
*''Estimation of Linear Functionals on Sobolev Spaces with Application to Fourier Transforms and Spline Interpolation.'' Bramble, James H., and Stephen R. Hilbert.  ''SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis'' (Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics) (Vol. 7, No. 1 (Mar., 1970)): 112–124.
*''A Mollifier Useful for Approximations in Sobolev Spaces and Some Applications to Approximating Solutions of Differential Equations''. Hilbert, Stephen. ''Mathematics of Computation'' (American Mathematical Society) (Vol. 27, No. 121 (Jan., 1973)): 81–89.
